blocks.text: In this chapter, students will learn the fundamentals of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) using Python. They will explore key OOP concepts like classes and objects to model real-world entities in code. The chapter covers encapsulation, which helps protect data and ensure privacy, and inheritance, allowing for code reuse and extension. Students will also study polymorphism to create flexible, adaptable programs. These concepts will help students develop well-structured and maintainable Python applications. By the end of the chapter, students will be proficient in applying OOP principles to design efficient and scalable programs.

Object-Oriented Programming is a method of designing programs using objects and classes. Each object represents a real-world entity with specific properties and behaviors. Classes act as templates for creating multiple objects with similar characteristics. OOP emphasizes encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism to manage data and behavior efficiently. This approach helps in modeling real-world problems in programming.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Create a chart comparing procedural programming and OOP. Have students explain scenarios where OOP is more useful.
Benefits of OOP: Modularity, Reusability, and Easier Maintenance

OOP allows code to be divided into modules, making it easier to manage. Classes and objects can be reused in multiple programs or parts of a program, reducing repetition. Programs built with OOP are easier to maintain and update because changes in one part do not affect the entire system. The structure of OOP supports scalability and adaptability in software development. It also improves collaboration by making code more understandable and organized.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Object-Oriented Programming helps programmers think in terms of real-life objects, like students or cars, making programs easier to understand and manage.
